commit_message:
[GPU] Fix integer reduction identities at the element bit width

Build signed extrema and all-ones integer reduction identities with APInt
at the element width. Separate signed and unsigned min/max identities and
use all ones for AND. Keep floating-point cases and index attribute storage
width unchanged.

Extend the existing common and AMD wide-shuffle tests to check the
identity used by each reduction across i8/i16/i32/i64.

Fixes #25153.

Assisted-by: OpenAI Codex
Signed-off-by: Demetrios Agourakis <demetrios@agourakis.med.br>

Bump cpp-linter/cpp-linter-action from 2.23.1 to 2.24.0 in the github-actions group (#25175) Bumps the github-actions group with 1 update: [cpp-linter/cpp-linter-action](https://github.com/cpp-linter/cpp-linter-action). Updates `cpp-linter/cpp-linter-action` from 2.23.1 to 2.24.0
Release notes

Sourced from cpp-linter/cpp-linter-action's releases.

v2.24.0

Behavior changes

  • ignore: build now only skips build/ at the repo root. Earlier versions also skipped nested folders such as src/build/, which was a bug. To skip every build folder, use ignore: '**/build'.
  • A relative database path is now resolved against the workspace (the working directory), not against repo-root. repo-root must be inside the workspace.
  • When the action downloads clang-format or clang-tidy (on Windows, or when the runner doesn't have the requested version), it now gets the newest patch release of that major version (for example, 14.0.6 instead of 14.0.0), together with clang's resource headers.

Improvements

  • windows-11-arm runners work now: cpp-linter no longer depends on pygit2, which has no Windows arm64 wheel.
  • A repo-root that is a sub-folder of the git repository works now.
  • Comments and reviews are posted through git-bot-feedback, which fixes the API URLs on GitHub Enterprise Server.

🐛 Bug fixes

  • fix: pass action inputs to run steps through env by @​shenxianpeng in #508

📝 Documentation updates

commit_message:
[Python] Add `__index__` support to HAL enums (#25163)

HAL enums implement `__int__`, but `nanobind 2.15` rejects them for
integer arguments and bitwise operations. Flag enums are now marked with is_arithmetic() + is_flag(), to avoid implementing any special members.

---------

commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] Preserve dynamic reshape types when folding unit dimensions (#25179)

`DropUnitDimsFromCollapseOfExpand` derived the new `expand_shape` result
type
from `getConstantIntValue` on the `output_shape` operands. When a
dimension was
dynamic in the type but supplied by an `arith.constant`, the new type
became
static while the value was still passed as a dynamic operand, producing
invalid
IR. Take the dims from the original result type instead, which keeps
type and operands consistent.

Co-authored-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>

commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] Preserve dynamic reshape types when folding unit dimensions (#25179)

`DropUnitDimsFromCollapseOfExpand` derived the new `expand_shape` result
type
from `getConstantIntValue` on the `output_shape` operands. When a
dimension was
dynamic in the type but supplied by an `arith.constant`, the new type
became
static while the value was still passed as a dynamic operand, producing
invalid
IR. Take the dims from the original result type instead, which keeps
type and operands consistent.

Co-authored-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>

Co-authored-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>

`DropUnitDimsFromCollapseOfExpand` derived the new `expand_shape` result
type
from `getConstantIntValue` on the `output_shape` operands. When a
dimension was
dynamic in the type but supplied by an `arith.constant`, the new type
became
static while the value was still passed as a dynamic operand, producing
invalid
IR. Take the dims from the original result type instead, which keeps
type and operands consistent.

Co-authored-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>

Co-authored-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>

commit_message:
[Docs] Add security policy

Adds SECURITY.md, which LF AI & Data requires and which the OpenSSF Best
Practices badge criteria refer to. It covers how to report a
vulnerability privately, how reports are handled and on what timeline,
which versions receive fixes, the security model and its trust
boundaries, issues that are not vulnerabilities, guidance for using IREE
securely, and the principles CI and release changes must preserve.

The structure follows the PyTorch and oneDNN security policies.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Tobias Fuchs <fuchs@roofline.ai>

Practices badge criteria refer to. It covers how to report a
vulnerability privately, how reports are handled and on what timeline,
which versions receive fixes, the security model and its trust
boundaries, issues that are not vulnerabilities, guidance for using IREE
securely, and the principles CI and release changes must preserve.

The structure follows the PyTorch and oneDNN security policies.

Bump cpp-linter/cpp-linter-action from 2.23.1 to 2.24.0 in the github-actions group (#25175) Bumps the github-actions group with 1 update: [cpp-linter/cpp-linter-action](https://github.com/cpp-linter/cpp-linter-action). Updates `cpp-linter/cpp-linter-action` from 2.23.1 to 2.24.0
Release notes

Sourced from cpp-linter/cpp-linter-action's releases.

v2.24.0

Behavior changes

  • ignore: build now only skips build/ at the repo root. Earlier versions also skipped nested folders such as src/build/, which was a bug. To skip every build folder, use ignore: '**/build'.
  • A relative database path is now resolved against the workspace (the working directory), not against repo-root. repo-root must be inside the workspace.
  • When the action downloads clang-format or clang-tidy (on Windows, or when the runner doesn't have the requested version), it now gets the newest patch release of that major version (for example, 14.0.6 instead of 14.0.0), together with clang's resource headers.

Improvements

  • windows-11-arm runners work now: cpp-linter no longer depends on pygit2, which has no Windows arm64 wheel.
  • A repo-root that is a sub-folder of the git repository works now.
  • Comments and reviews are posted through git-bot-feedback, which fixes the API URLs on GitHub Enterprise Server.

🐛 Bug fixes

  • fix: pass action inputs to run steps through env by @​shenxianpeng in #508

📝 Documentation updates

  • docs: add a cpp-linter badge section and pin the badge workflow to a release by @​shenxianpeng in #510
  • docs: give the home page a real title instead of a description by @​shenxianpeng in #506
  • docs: fix outdated permissions and example workflows by @​shenxianpeng in #505
  • docs: add Google Analytics and a descriptive home page title by @​shenxianpeng in #504
  • docs: add a Sponsors section to the README by @​shenxianpeng in #497
  • docs: rework the README to the org layout and move required tools to the docs by @​shenxianpeng in #493
  • docs: drop the note that thread comments are disabled on private repositories by @​shenxianpeng in #492
  • docs: fix the usage example and the list of users by @​shenxianpeng in #491
  • docs: let the shared styles bring the fonts by @​shenxianpeng in #489
  • docs: load the shared styles and rename the hub link by @​shenxianpeng in #487

👻 Maintenance

  • chore: update filelock to 4.2.4 for its security fixes by @​shenxianpeng in #514
  • chore: limit workflow token permissions by @​shenxianpeng in #507
  • chore: add a repo-level FUNDING.yml by @​shenxianpeng in #498
  • chore: update the pre-commit hooks quarterly by @​shenxianpeng in #490

commit_message:
Bump cpp-linter/cpp-linter-action from 2.23.1 to 2.24.0 in the github-actions group (#25175) Bumps the github-actions group with 1 update: [cpp-linter/cpp-linter-action](https://github.com/cpp-linter/cpp-linter-action). Updates `cpp-linter/cpp-linter-action` from 2.23.1 to 2.24.0
Release notes

Sourced from cpp-linter/cpp-linter-action's releases.

v2.24.0

Behavior changes

  • ignore: build now only skips build/ at the repo root. Earlier versions also skipped nested folders such as src/build/, which was a bug. To skip every build folder, use ignore: '**/build'.
  • A relative database path is now resolved against the workspace (the working directory), not against repo-root. repo-root must be inside the workspace.
  • When the action downloads clang-format or clang-tidy (on Windows, or when the runner doesn't have the requested version), it now gets the newest patch release of that major version (for example, 14.0.6 instead of 14.0.0), together with clang's resource headers.

Improvements

  • windows-11-arm runners work now: cpp-linter no longer depends on pygit2, which has no Windows arm64 wheel.
  • A repo-root that is a sub-folder of the git repository works now.
  • Comments and reviews are posted through git-bot-feedback, which fixes the API URLs on GitHub Enterprise Server.

commit_message:
[VM] Fix ref ownership in branch remaps (#24781)

Branch remaps selected MOVE using `isLastRealValueUse`, whose result
accounts for uses across all successors. A use on one successor
therefore prevented ownership transfer on another mutually exclusive
successor, leaving an extra owning reference on the taken path.

Use target-block liveness to select MOVE independently for each
successor. If one occurrence of a repeated operand is coalesced with its
destination, prevent the other remaps from using MOVE; otherwise a MOVE
would clear the coalesced register.

Add register allocation tests for both cases and an LLVM CPU end-to-end
regression that executes both selector paths with indirect command
buffers disabled.

Fixes #24753

[VM] Fix ref ownership in branch remaps (#24781)

Branch remaps selected MOVE using `isLastRealValueUse`, whose result
accounts for uses across all successors. A use on one successor
therefore prevented ownership transfer on another mutually exclusive
successor, leaving an extra owning reference on the taken path.

Use target-block liveness to select MOVE independently for each
successor. If one occurrence of a repeated operand is coalesced with its
destination, prevent the other remaps from using MOVE; otherwise a MOVE
would clear the coalesced register.

Add register allocation tests for both cases and an LLVM CPU end-to-end
regression that executes both selector paths with indirect command
buffers disabled.

commit_message:
[GPU] Fix integer reduction identities at the element bit width (#25176)

The reduction helper builds integer min/max identities from fixed
`int64_t` limits and uses `1` for AND. Those values can change meaning
when converted to a narrower type. The shared signed/unsigned cases also
give the wrong identities for unsigned `i64` reductions.

This patch builds the identities with `APInt` at the element's bit width
and gives signed and unsigned min/max their own cases. Unsigned minimum
and AND use all ones; unsigned maximum uses zero. The floating-point
cases and index-attribute storage width stay unchanged.

Fixes #25153.

The added cases live in the existing common and AMD wide-shuffle tests.
They cover `i8`, `i16`, `i32`, and `i64`, and check that the reduction
actually uses the expected constant. The existing scan, mask, and
argcompare checks pass too.

Assisted-by: OpenAI Codex

Signed-off-by: Demetrios Agourakis <demetrios@agourakis.med.br>
name: linux_x64_gcc

commit_message:
[VM] Fix ref ownership in branch remaps

Branch remaps selected MOVE using `isLastRealValueUse`, whose result accounts
for uses across all successors. A use on one successor therefore prevented
ownership transfer on another mutually exclusive successor, leaving an extra
owning reference on the taken path.

Use target-block liveness to select MOVE independently for each successor. If
one occurrence of a repeated operand is coalesced with its destination,
prevent the other remaps from using MOVE; otherwise a MOVE would clear the
coalesced register.

Add register allocation tests for both cases and an LLVM CPU end-to-end
regression that executes both selector paths with indirect command buffers
disabled.

Fixes #24753

Co-authored-by: OpenAI <noreply@openai.com>
Signed-off-by: zhangpan <98025960+zhangpan2001@users.noreply.github.com>

commit_message:
[VM] Fix ref ownership in branch remaps

Branch remaps selected MOVE using `isLastRealValueUse`, whose result accounts
for uses across all successors. A use on one successor therefore prevented
ownership transfer on another mutually exclusive successor, leaving an extra
owning reference on the taken path.

Use target-block liveness to select MOVE independently for each successor. If
one occurrence of a repeated operand is coalesced with its destination,
prevent the other remaps from using MOVE; otherwise a MOVE would clear the
coalesced register.

Add register allocation tests for both cases and an LLVM CPU end-to-end
regression that executes both selector paths with indirect command buffers
disabled.

Fixes #24753

commit_message:
[Runtime] Use libc monotonic clock on Emscripten (#25165)

While building with Emscripten 6x (latest emscripten), `clock_now_ns` is an undefined symbol. Emscripten currently takes the freestanding Wasm clock path, although it already provides `clock_gettime`.

Use the existing libc `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` path for Emscripten.

---------

commit_message:
[GPU] Fix integer reduction identities at the element bit width (#25176)

The reduction helper builds integer min/max identities from fixed
`int64_t` limits and uses `1` for AND. Those values can change meaning
when converted to a narrower type. The shared signed/unsigned cases also
give the wrong identities for unsigned `i64` reductions.

This patch builds the identities with `APInt` at the element's bit width
and gives signed and unsigned min/max their own cases. Unsigned minimum
and AND use all ones; unsigned maximum uses zero. The floating-point
cases and index-attribute storage width stay unchanged.

Fixes #25153.

The added cases live in the existing common and AMD wide-shuffle tests.
They cover `i8`, `i16`, `i32`, and `i64`, and check that the reduction
actually uses the expected constant. The existing scan, mask, and
argcompare checks pass too.

commit_message:
[VM] Fix ref ownership in branch remaps (#24781)

Branch remaps selected MOVE using `isLastRealValueUse`, whose result
accounts for uses across all successors. A use on one successor
therefore prevented ownership transfer on another mutually exclusive
successor, leaving an extra owning reference on the taken path.

Use target-block liveness to select MOVE independently for each
successor. If one occurrence of a repeated operand is coalesced with its
destination, prevent the other remaps from using MOVE; otherwise a MOVE
would clear the coalesced register.

Add register allocation tests for both cases and an LLVM CPU end-to-end
regression that executes both selector paths with indirect command
buffers disabled.

Fixes #24753

Signed-off-by: zhangpan <98025960+zhangpan2001@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: OpenAI <noreply@openai.com>

commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] Preserve dynamic reshape types when folding unit dimensions (#25179)

`DropUnitDimsFromCollapseOfExpand` derived the new `expand_shape` result
type
from `getConstantIntValue` on the `output_shape` operands. When a
dimension was
dynamic in the type but supplied by an `arith.constant`, the new type
became
static while the value was still passed as a dynamic operand, producing
invalid
IR. Take the dims from the original result type instead, which keeps
type and operands consistent.

Co-authored-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>

[Python] Add `__index__` support to HAL enums (#25163)

HAL enums implement `__int__`, but `nanobind 2.15` rejects them for
integer arguments and bitwise operations. Flag enums are now marked with is_arithmetic() + is_flag(), to avoid implementing any special members.
